annotations.text:
Your four asks, applied:

1. Project name is now the headline; vendor sits under it; the shipment number drops to the meta line.
2. "PO" → "Ref#" everywhere.
3. Timestamps on every stage that has one — including In Transit, which reads the truck's departure from the pickup dock (data we already receive and have never shown).
4. Green check on Delivered, on the status line and the last dot.

Pick a header in the Header artboard and I'll build it for real.

Why "Out for Delivery" is gone:

TAI has sent exactly four statuses in 73 shipments — Delivered, Committed, In Transit, Canceled. "Out for Delivery" has never arrived once, so that dot could never light up, never be the current stage, and never carry a time. It filled in retroactively on delivered loads and sat grey on live ones.

The portal's delivery rail already drops it for the same reason.

Built at the PORTAL's scale, not the tracking page's — 300px cards, 11px dots, 10px labels, 1px connectors, its own space/type tokens. Copying the tracking page's pixels would have made these cards wrong.

Colour is by TOKEN, not by hex: --status-success is #177A41 in light (raised for AA) and #3FD68F in dark, and the tick's stroke is --bg-surface so it reads on either. The only difference between the two panes is the token block; the markup is identical.

What's new vs. today's DeliveryRail: the green delivered state, real stage times, Ref# wording, and document tiles.
